name: Piracetam
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: About 90% of piracetam is excreted unchanged in urine, so the dose falls in steps with creatinine clearance (CrCl): two-thirds at 50–79, one-third at 30–49 and one-sixth (once daily) below 30 mL/min. It is contraindicated in end-stage kidney disease, and hemodialysis removes 50% to 60%. It also inhibits platelet aggregation. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European core safety profile uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault, ×0.85 for women).
chip: Dose by CrCl; contraindicated in ESKD

bands.recommendation: CrCl >80: usual dose in 2 to 4 divided doses (e.g., 2.4 to 4.8 g/day; up to 24 g/day for cortical myoclonus). CrCl 60–79: two-thirds of the usual dose in 2 or 3 divided doses (CSP).
CrCl 50–59: two-thirds of the usual daily dose in 2 or 3 divided doses. CrCl 30–49: one-third of the usual daily dose in 2 divided doses (CSP).
CrCl <30: one-sixth of the usual daily dose as a single daily dose (CSP).

CrCl <30: one-sixth of the usual daily dose once daily. End-stage kidney disease: contraindicated (CSP). Equating CrCl <15 with end-stage disease is our judgment; we keep it red because piracetam is renally cleared, of marginal benefit and affects platelets in a population prone to uremic bleeding.

hd.text: Contraindicated in end-stage kidney disease (CSP). Hemodialysis removes 50% to 60% (dialyzer extraction), useful in overdose.

crrt.text: Not appropriate; contraindicated in end-stage kidney disease and no data in acute kidney injury.

monitoring: Creatinine clearance regularly in older adults and long-term use. Bleeding risk (platelet inhibition): caution with anticoagulants, antiplatelets, ulcer, recent surgery or hemorrhagic stroke. Do not stop abruptly in myoclonus (CSP 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Dyslexia from 8 years; sickle cell crises from 3 years (limited data 1 to 3 years) (CSP).
pediatric.usual_dose: Dyslexia (8 years and older): about 3.2 g/day in 2 doses. Sickle cell: 160 mg/kg/day orally (prophylaxis); 300 mg/kg/day intravenously (crisis) (CSP).

renal.recommendation: Normal kidney function: usual pediatric doses (CSP).
